newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees wave of new enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees wave of new enquiry.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh enquiry at the start of the week as a number of new account orders emerged but no fixtures, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Seabon was open on account for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from the EU excluding UK to Iran for May.

Geepee was open on account for 12,500 tonnes in bags from Port Sudan to Chittagong for prompt/onwards and Middle East Charterers quoted for 7,000 tonnes in bags from Djibouti to Somalia for April 28/May 5.
Czarnikow Rionda was still open with its 9/12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to west Africa/east Africa/Colombo for prompt/May sipment.
It was also open with a 14,000-tonne east coast Mexico bagged cargo for May shipment to east Mediterranean with west/east Africa and Colombo options.
Secretan produced its usual spate of bagged enquiries, mainly from European origins.
Three of the orders were for Algeria -- 3,000 tonnes from Antwerp and 2,000 from Gijon, both for this week, and 6,000 from Gijon for May 15/30.
It also quoted for 4/7,000 tonnes from Rouen/Hamburg range to Batumi for May 5/15 and 5/10,000 from east coast Mexico to Nouakchott/Angola range for 8/15 May.

Lorico repeated its 16,000 tonnes order from Cuba to Alexandria and Louis Dreyfus quoted for 22,625 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Black Sea for May 10/15 and a 5,000 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Maputo for May 12/16.
Genoc was in the market with 14/15,700 tonnes of bulk sugar from Goa to US Gulf/Atlantic with California option for May 15/25 and 25/30,000 tonnes from Cuba to Egyptian Med/Black Sea/Baltic for May.
Shipbrokers said Genoc was still open with its order for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Pland to Red Sea/Pakistan/Colombo for proimpt/10 days notice.
